Your fifty rupee stock could be a trap. I tested ten stocks under fifty rupees. Only five passed.
Five rules. Profit every quarter. Low debt. Return on equity above ten percent. No promoter pledge. Growing profit.

The five that failed. Yes Bank, return on equity just seven percent. Trident, shrinking profit. IRB, heavy debt. JP Power, seventy three percent of promoter shares pledged. EaseMyTrip, losses in three of four quarters.
Now the five that passed. And no, a low price is not the reason.
Syncom Formulations, pharma, twenty rupees. Return on equity seventeen percent, almost no debt. Sagility, healthcare services, forty five rupees. Profit up eighty six percent a year.

Indian Overseas Bank, twenty nine rupees. Return on equity fifteen percent, net bad loans just zero point one six percent. Central Bank of India, also twenty nine. Profit growing forty percent a year.
And Suzlon, wind energy, thirty seven rupees. Return on equity forty percent, almost debt free. But promoters own only twelve percent.
Passing is not a buy signal. Each has a catch, like government stake sales or one-time income. Check the latest results first.
